newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault sees tough H2 for cars, trucks.
newsitem.headline: Renault sees tough H2 for cars, trucks.

text.p: Renault SA said it expected its car activity to show only a slight improvement in its operating results for the second half of 1996 from the second half of 1995, when the car division lost money.
Renault said in a statement that it expected an operating loss in its commercial vehicles division in the second half.
"Prospects for the passenger car market in the second half of the year are uncertain," Renault said.

"In France, in particular, in a context characterised by sluggish consumer spending and a very acute sensitivity to prices, the automobile market should remain strong in the third quarter until the termination of the automobile quality bonus on September 30, but there is a risk of a significant decline in the fourth quarter," it said.
"Under these conditions, operating income of the automobile division would only show a slight improvement compared with the second half of 1995," it said.
"In the area of commercial vehicles, Renault will have to contend with the combination of a continued downturn in the cycle in the United States and marked slowing in the European markets," it said.

"Consequently, the operating income of the commercial vehicles division would be negative, while the finance division would report an operating profit in line with that of the previous half-year periods," it said.
The car unit lost 911 million francs in the first half of 1996. It lost 1.35 billion francs in the second half of 1995 and showed a 358 million operating profit in the first half of 1995.

The commercial vehicles division had operating income of 26 million francs in the first half of 1996, compared with income of 459 million francs in the second half of 1995 and income of 519 million francs in the first half of 1995.
